Answer.description: The answer to a question: P(fail).

noul.description: The probability that the subject fails the decision, from 0 to 1.

CacheRef.description: The directory a provider may keep derived results in between runs.

dir.description:
Absolute path of a directory the host owns, `.lighthouse/cache/<plugin
id>/`. The provider reads and writes only inside it and its results are
the same with or without it.

Call.description: Params and result types of one method.

Call2.description: Params and result types of one method.

Call3.description: Params and result types of one method.

agent.description: Runs as an agent that edits files (`lighthouse/edit`).

Comment.description: A comment of the file. Adjacent line comments are one comment.

attached_to.description: Id of the symbol the comment is the documentation of, when known.

text.description:
Source text including the comment markers (`//`, `/* */`, `#`); the
lines of one comment are joined by `\n`.

Context.description: Host-side settings that accompany an index request.

cache.description:
Where the provider may cache derived results; absent when the host runs
without a cache.

options.description: Per-language options from `[languages.<id>]`, keyed by language id.

overlays.description:
Texts that replace requested files, see [`Overlay`]; absent when there
are none.

Conventions.description: Layout conventions of a language that the host cannot infer from its files.

constructor_prefixes.description:
Name prefixes that make a function a constructor, such as `New` in Go
or `new` in Rust; a name is a constructor when it is a prefix or a
prefix followed by a new word. The project may replace them in
`[languages.<id>] constructorPrefixes`.

test_naming.description:
How tests are named after the symbols they own. The project may
replace each part in `[languages.<id>] testNaming`.

CreateFineTuningJobRequest.description:
The body of OpenAI's fine-tuning job creation (`POST /v1/fine_tuning/jobs`),
which `lighthouse/train` takes verbatim. `training_file` is the digest
(`sha256:<hex>`) of a JSON Lines file of [`TrainingLine`]s in the host's
dataset store; `metadata` names the `decision`, the `datasets` directory
the file is in (`<hex>.jsonl` under `sha256/`) and the `dir` the artifact
goes to.

options.description: The `options` of the project's provider. Not part of OpenAI's body.

Criteria.description:
The two sides of a yes/no question: `true` is that the subject fails the
decision, `false` that it passes.

Criterion.description: What a criterion means, and what it looks like.

Edge.description: A directed relation between two code-model nodes.

site.description:
Where the reference occurs: the span of the identifier that names the
target (capability `reference-sites`). The same relation used at
several places is one edge per place. Added in 0.1 before 1.0.

to.description:
A module path, a symbol id, or a kind-less symbol id
(`module::owner::name`) that names exactly one symbol.

EdgeKind.description: The relation an edge states between its endpoints.

EditParams.description:
Params of `lighthouse/edit`: the agent changes the files of `dir` as the
prompt says.

dir.description: The directory it runs in and may change.

model.description: The agent asked: the part of the reference after the provider.

prompt.description: What the agent is asked to do, as plain text.

events.description:
What the agent read, searched, listed, edited and ran, when the plugin
can tell.

said.description: What the agent said about it.

Event.description: One body event and where it is.

EventKind.description:
What a function body does that a rule may flag; the same kinds for every
language, each only where the language has it.

oneOf.description:
Go: a call of the builtin `panic`. Rust: the `panic!`, `unreachable!`,
`todo!` and `unimplemented!` macros (the detail names the macro).

Rust: a `.unwrap()` or `.expect(..)` call on any receiver (the detail
names the method).

Go: `==` or `!=` where one operand has type `error` and the other is
not nil (the detail is the operand text).
Go: a type assertion or type switch on an `error` value.

Go: `fmt.Errorf` given an `error` argument whose format has no `%w`
(the detail is the verb used).

Example.description: One valid or invalid example of a decision.

FileInfo.description: Identity and classification of an indexed file.

facts.description:
What the provider says of the file besides that, by name, for a
program to name as `{file.<name>}`: the `edition` of a Rust file's
crate.

FileRef.description: A file to index; the plugin reads its content from disk.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the file content, lowercase hex.

FineTuneJobError.description: Why a job failed, in OpenAI's words.

FineTuneMethod.description: The method of a fine-tuning job.

FineTuneSupervisedMethod.description: OpenAI's supervised fine-tuning method, with optional OpenAI parameters.

FineTuningJob.description:
OpenAI's `FineTuningJob`. Over stdio `lighthouse/train` answers with the
final one: `fine_tuned_model` is the reference (`learned@sha256:<hex>`) and the
first of `result_files` is a JSON file of the metrics.

FineTuningJobStatus.description: How far a fine-tuning job is.

Flow.description:
A control-flow construct and the number of enclosing nesting constructs,
nested functions included, around it.

arms.description: `switch`: arms other than the default arm.

returning.description: `switch`: every arm, default included, is a single return.

FlowKind.description: Normalized control-flow construct, the same for every language.

comments.description:
Comments of the file in source order. Added in 0.1 before 1.0; a
plugin that does not know comments omits the field.

FunctionSummary.description: Size and shape measures of one function or method, keyed by its symbol id.

constructs.description:
The function builds a value of its owner type without taking one: an
associated function without a receiver that returns `Self` or the
owner. Added in 0.1 before 1.0.

events.description:
What the body does that a rule may flag, in source order; only a
function with a body has any. Added in 0.1 before 1.0; empty when the
plugin reports none.

forwards_to.description:
Target of the call the body consists of when it passes the receiver and
every parameter on, in order.

implementation.description:
The function implements a method that a trait or interface declares
elsewhere (a method of a trait impl in Rust). Added in 0.1 before 1.0.

manual_assertions.description:
Checks of a test file's function written out by hand: an `if` that
compares and whose only effect is to fail the test. Added in 0.1
before 1.0; zero when the plugin does not count them.

max_nesting.description: Deepest level of nested constructs; a flat body is 0.

signature.description:
The types of the parameters and results, receiver excluded, one entry
per occurrence in order. Added in 0.1 before 1.0; empty when the plugin
does not report types.

top_level.description: Statements directly in the body, not in nested blocks.

Implementation.description:
Name and version of a peer: `clientInfo` of the host, `serverInfo` of the
plugin. For diagnostics, except that the plugin's name is its id.

Incomplete.description: Part of the request that was not analyzed; "not checked" is not "passed".

path.description: Project-relative path; absent when the gap is not tied to one file.

IndexParams.description:
Index request. A provider receives every file of one language in one
request and decides which packages or modules it must load to analyze
them; analysis scope is never narrowed to a subset of the project.

language.description: Id of the language the files belong to.

IndexResult.description:
A plugin's answer to `index`: one fragment per analyzed file plus what could
not be analyzed. A file is never silently dropped.

fragments.description: One fragment per analyzed file, ordered by path.

incomplete.description:
Files or scopes that could not be analyzed. A file listed here may
still have a fragment with whatever could be recovered.

notices.description: Messages that leave the analysis complete.

InitializeParams.description:
First request, sent by the host. Fields of protocol messages are camelCase;
fields of the code model are snake_case.

workspaceFolders.description: The project root; exactly one folder for now.

InitializeResult.description:
A plugin's answer to `initialize`: who it is, which protocol it speaks, and
what it offers.

protocolVersion.description: Must equal the host's protocol version.

serverInfo.description:
`name` is the plugin id; it must equal the `id` of its
`lighthouse-plugin.toml`.

prompt.description: What the model is told; the requirement unless the check says more.

ListModelResponse.description: OpenAI's list object of models: how a plugin says which it offers.

Model.description:
One model: OpenAI's model object, with what Lighthouse adds
(`version`, `cost`, `deterministic`, `abstains`).

Module.description: Package, directory or namespace; `path` identifies it project-wide.

name.description: Name the language gives the module, such as a Go package name.

test_of.description: Path of the module whose public surface this one tests from outside.

Neighbor.description: A symbol near the subject: a caller or callee.

text.description: The neighbor's source when it is in the subject's file, truncated.

Node.description: An edge endpoint: a whole module or one symbol.

Overlay.description:
The text that stands in for a file: a provider reads it instead of the
file on disk, and must not read the disk for that path. Hosts send overlays
for requested files only, as a fix run verifies edits before writing them.

Position.description: 1-based line and column; the column counts bytes.

ProjectRef.description: The project an index request belongs to.

root.description: Absolute path of the project root.

ProviderManifest.description:
What a language provider declares: the language it indexes, how the host
routes files to it and what it guarantees. A plugin's `initialize` result
lists one per language.

capabilities.description:
Known values: `semantic-edges`, `extent`, `reference-sites`,
`complete-references`. Hosts
ignore unknown values.

fallback.description: A fallback language claims a file only when no other language does.

globs.description:
Project-relative path globs; `*` and `?` never cross `/`, a `**`
component matches any number of directories.

priority.description: Among providers matching a file, the higher priority wins.

Question.description: One yes/no question: System One's `noul`, the probability of yes.

Resolution.description: How reliable an edge's target is.

oneOf.description: The target comes from type information.
The target comes from names alone.

A guess: the edge says the source may use the target, never that it
does. Analyzers that count calls or dependencies ignore such edges; a
rule asking whether something might be used may honor them.

ServerCapabilities.description: What a plugin offers: the languages it indexes and the models it serves.

models.description:
The models the plugin offers, as OpenAI's list object; empty for a
language plugin.

Signature.description:
The parameter and result types of a function, receiver excluded. A Rust
tuple result is one `results` entry.

State.description: The part of a subject a model reads: TypeSafe System One's `state`.

Supports.description: What a model can do, as OpenAI's model object lists it.

Symbol.description: A named declaration; `id` is unique across the project.

extent.description:
The whole declaration, from its first leading doc comment, attribute
or annotation to its last token (capability `extent`). A spec of a
grouped declaration, such as one constant of a Go `const (...)` block,
has the spec's own lines. Added in 0.1 before 1.0.

file.description: Project-relative path of the declaring file.

optional.description:
A field a caller may leave out: a pointer, slice, map, function,
channel or interface in Go; an `Option`, a collection or a
`#[serde(default)]` field in Rust. Added in 0.1 before 1.0.

owner.description: Id of the enclosing type or interface.

role.description:
Set on the declarations of test files whose purpose the language can
tell; test entry points are `test` symbols and carry none.

type_ref.description: The type of a field. Added in 0.1 before 1.0.

SymbolKind.description: What a symbol declares; the kebab-case name is the `#kind` suffix of its id.

SymbolRole.description:
What a declaration of a test file is for. Added in 0.1 before 1.0; a
plugin that cannot tell omits it.

oneOf.description:
Test code that checks on behalf of tests, such as a function that takes
the test framework's handle.

Test data and code that builds it: types, constants, variables and
functions that need no handle.

SystemOneRequest.description:
The body of TypeSafe's System One API (`POST /v1/systemone`), for one
subject and the decisions judged on it, keyed by decision id.

model.description: The model asked: the part of the reference after the provider.

options.description: Provider options, omitted when empty and stripped by HTTP providers.

SystemOneResponse.description:
Result of `lighthouse/classify`: System One's response. Every question
asked is answered; a missing answer is an abstention.

model.description: The model that answered, with its version when it has one.

TestCase.description: A test symbol and the symbols it exercises.

targets.description: Symbols the test calls or references, as edge targets.

TestNaming.description:
The convention that ties a top-level test function to the public symbol it
owns: Go writes `TestGet` and `TestGet_Missing`, Rust writes `get` in
snake case and tests a whole crate from `tests/`.

ancestors.description:
The tests of a module that tests an ancestor module also name the
symbols of the nested module: the integration tests of a crate test
all of it.

prefix.description:
Prefix of an owner test's name (`Test` in Go); a test without it is
not an owner test.

snake_case.description: Names are compared in snake case (Rust tests are `snake_case`).

variants.description: `TestGet_Missing` is a second owner of `Get`, not a case of it.

TestStyle.description: How a test enumerates its cases: one body over a data table, or separate scenarios.

Tool.description:
What an agent did with a tool: the kinds of its work that a fix report
tells apart.

oneOf.description: Searched file contents for a pattern.

ToolEvent.description: One thing an agent did, as its harness reported it.

outside.description:
It was about a path outside the directory the agent ran in. The host
sets this and drops the path, so that no path of the machine reaches a
report; a plugin leaves it out.

path.description:
The file or directory it was about, relative to the directory the
agent ran in, as the host normalizes it. A plugin may send it absolute
or relative to that directory.

pattern.description: What a `search` looked for, or the glob of a `list`.

TypeRef.description: A type as a signature or a field writes it.

exported.description: Whether that named type is visible outside its module, when known.

symbol.description:
The project type it names, as a kind-less symbol id (`module::name`),
with pointers, references and aliases stripped; a slice or map names
nothing.

text.description:
The type as written, normalized: Go prints it with the full package
path as qualifier (`context.Context`, `*example.com/m/x.T`,
`[]string`); Rust prints the path text without whitespace
(`Option<Ctx>`, `&mut Builder`).

Visibility.description:
Who may use a symbol, as its language defines it; `internal` means visible
within a bounded unit such as a crate, not outside it.

WorkspaceFolder.description: A root of the workspace, as in LSP.

uri.description: `file://` URI of the directory, percent-encoded as RFC 8089 says.

description: Every method with its params and result. Exists to anchor the schema.
title: Methods
